## 1. Introduction

This  Fitness  to  Practise  Policy  has  been  developed  in  recognition  of  the  duty  of  the  Faculty  of Science  and  Computing,  ('The  Faculty'),  and  namely  the  Department  of  Pharmacy  ('The Department') at SETU ('the University') to support students to fulfil programme requirements, ensure  patient  and  public  safety,  and  to  prepare  students  for  future  professional  practice. Specified  programmes  of  study  within  the  Department  of  Pharmacy  will  be  governed  by  a requirement  that  students  demonstrate  their  Fitness  to  Practise  on  programmes  recognised, regulated, and  accredited  by  Professional,  Statutory  or  Regulatory  Pharmacy  bodies.  The Department reserves the right to amend the range of programmes to which this Policy applies, as deemed  necessary.  A  student's  fitness  to  practise  is  determined  by  a  combination  of  Garda vetting, self-disclosure, adherence to the Department of Pharmacy Professional Code of Conduct for Student Pharmacists and their professional performance through all years of their programme. The policy has been developed to ensure the programme meets the Accreditation Standards of the Pharmaceutical Society of Ireland and is developed from and aligned to those effective within SETU in healthcare related programmes.

## 2. Purpose

Fitness to Practise is concerned with issues that affect the ability of a person to practise in their profession. Here, it ensures that the pharmacy professional has the skills, knowledge, good health, character, and ability to practise safely and effectively and includes the requirement to conform to certain standards of conduct. Good health, in this instance, means that the person is capable of safe and effective practise without supervision. It does not mean the absence of any disability or health condition.

This  Policy  is  intended  to  respond  to  and  manage  concerns  regarding  a  student's  fitness  to practise and/or professional suitability, collectively referred to herein as 'Fitness to Practise'. This policy seeks to ensure that, in addition to having achieved the required academic standard and demonstrated  the  Core  Competencies  as  outlined  by  the  Core  Competency  Framework  for Pharmacists students also:

- Are not impeded to practise in their chosen profession by issues of ill health. Ill health is a long term, untreated or unacknowledged physical or mental health condition that impairs a person's ability to provide safe and effective practise without supervision. As above, it does not mean the absence of any disability or health condition.
- Conduct and behave themselves so as not to harm, or put at risk of harm, their patients, clients, service users, customers, colleagues, or the public.
- Conduct and behave themselves in a manner which will not harm the reputation of the University, their profession, or experiential learning practice partners.

Where  issues  of  concern  regarding  a student's Fitness  to  Practise  are  raised,  they  will  be investigated  and dealt with  in  accordance  with  the  Procedures  in this Policy.  Where  a  concern arises  amongst the  Department of Pharmacy programme team regarding a student's fitness  to practise, or is raised by a student, the issue is brought, in the first instance, to the Programme Director and/or the Practice Educator who will follow the process as outlined under this Fitness to Practise policy.

## 3. Scope

This  policy  applies  to  all  students  registered  on  the  5-Year  Master  of  Pharmacy  (MPharm) programme, or programmes defined within the Department of Pharmacy, which are deemed to have Fitness to Practise requirements. This policy shall be made generally available and published publicly via the University website. It will be provided to students in their handbook, on the VLE and discussed with students at induction and before each subsequent year of the programme.

Where a student has been found to be in breach of SETU Department of Pharmacy Professional Code of Conduct for Pharmacy students, or the APPEL Joint Schools of Pharmacy Code of Conduct, the Programme Director and/or Practice Educator, will notify the Head of the Department who will assess  the  breach.  It  may  be  deemed  that  the  breach  is  dealt  with  under  the  SETU  Code  of Conduct and Student Expected Behaviour Policy and Disciplinary Procedure or the SETU Student Academic  Misconduct  Policy  and  Disciplinary  Procedure  or  other  procedures  at  Faculty  and Department Level, in which cases these will be invoked. Alternatively, the Head of Department will invoke the Department of Pharmacy Fitness to Practise Policy, if required. As outlined in the SETU  Code  of  Conduct  and  Student  Expected  Behaviour  Policy  and  Disciplinary  Procedure,  a complaint  may  be  submitted  to  the  Complaints  Resolution  Officer  online,  in  the  event  that  an informal resolution is impossible or where the Complaint is of such a serious nature as to warrant this approach. Complaints will be investigated and resolved through respective University informal and formal disciplinary procedures.  If the breach is deemed by the Head of Department to be a Fitness to Practise breach, this policy will be followed.

Academic  integrity  misconduct  in  the  first  instance  will  be  dealt  with  through  the  Faculty  of Science and Computing Academic Integrity Procedures or the SETU Student Academic Misconduct Policy and Disciplinary Procedure. However, it may be deemed that this constitutes a breach that invokes a fitness to practise investigation.

Persistent absences from classes, late attendance or failure to adhere to the SETU Department of Pharmacy Attendance procedures may also lead to invocation of this policy. This policy therefore is aligned with and supported by these SETU procedures, which are available through the policy's links.

## 4. Principles

The paramount consideration in all Fitness to Practise matters is the safety and well-being of the student, staff, public, patients, clients, and service users. The University has a fundamental duty to ensure that its graduates are fit to enter their chosen profession and pose no undue risk to those they serve.

The  University  and  thus,  the  Department  of  Pharmacy,  endeavours  to  deal  with  any  issues regarding Fitness to Practise in a fair, prompt, transparent, and proportionate fashion and in a way that ensures a supportive learning environment, a positive student experience, and a safe working environment.

All individuals involved in the Fitness to Practise process will act impartially and must declare any actual, potential, or perceived conflicts of interest in line with the University's Conflict of Interest requirements.

Concerns about Fitness to  Practise will  be  acted  upon  promptly,  to  support  early  intervention. This policy may also provide a basis for counselling a student to discontinue a programme.

The  University  is  committed  to  protecting  the  privacy  rights  of  students  in  respect  to  the processing of their personal data and a copy of the University's privacy notice is available on the SETU website at SETU | Data Protection. The Department respects rights of confidentiality and the right of the student to withhold consent to a disclosure of sensitive information. However, it may be  necessary  to  breach  confidentiality  when  a  student's  mental  health  has  deteriorated  to  the extent  of  compromising  their  personal  safety,  when  a  student  is  at  risk  of  serious  abuse  or exploitation, when the student's behaviour is likely  to  adversely  affect  the  rights  and  safety  of others,  and/or  where  a  member  of  staff  would  be  liable  to  civil  or  criminal  procedure  if  the information were not disclosed. It may be necessary to discuss a Fitness to Practise concern with the  Child  and  Family  Agency,  An  Garda  Síochána,  or  other  third  parties  such  as  a  Professional, Regulatory and/or Statutory Body or a placement provider.

The University recognises its obligations to students under relevant legislation, including the Equal Status  Acts  2000-2018,  the  Data  Protection  Acts  1988-2018.  All  proceedings  will  be  conducted fairly, impartially, and objectively. Students will be afforded due process, including the right to be informed of allegations, to respond fully, present evidence, and to be accompanied or represented throughout  the  process.  A  student  is  presumed  innocent  until  concerns  are  upheld  based  on evidence. The University acknowledges that Fitness to Practise procedures can be challenging for students  and  commits  to  providing  access  to  appropriate  pastoral  care,  welfare  support,  and guidance on the process itself.

As part of its statutory annual reporting to the Pharmaceutical Society of Ireland, the Department must submit data on any Fitness to Practise cases. The Head of Department must report to the PSI any  'fitness  to  practise'  matters  which  could  impact  future  'fitness  to  practise'  when  the student/graduate is practising as a pharmacist.

The student may appeal the decision of the Fitness to Practise Committee to the President of the University as outlined in this Policy.

## 5. Application of the Policy

This  Policy  applies  to  students  who  are  registered  or  seek  to  be  registered  on  relevant programmes, including the Master of Pharmacy programme in the Department of Pharmacy and applies throughout their period of registration, both on and off campus. It is not limited to term time, experiential learning placement, or work-based learning.

In appropriate cases, the application of this Policy may lead to the suspension or termination of a student's registration on a relevant programme.

A  decision  made  under  this  Policy  concerning  Fitness  to  Practise  is  a  matter  for  professional judgment.  The  standard  of  proof  applied  at  every  stage  of  the  application  of  this  Policy  is  the balance of probabilities.

Matters dealt with under this Policy will be considered according to the individual circumstances. Whilst the Department anticipates that such cases will be exceptional, it reserves the right at any stage of proceedings and/or at any level of this Policy to vary the process it follows in dealing with a matter in the interests of fairness and/or health and safety.

Should a student be unwilling or unable to participate at any level of this Policy, or to attend a meeting, the Department may nonetheless follow this Policy where it is reasonable to do so. This includes  instances  where  the  student  has  been  legally  advised  not  to  attend  due  to  pending criminal proceedings. The Department and University may, where it is reasonable to do so, deal with issues based on written reports and/or statements in the absence of the student. In addition, the Department and University may consider any request from a student to proceed with meeting in their absence based on written reports and/or a written statement from the student.

The Department is not bound by the outcome of any third-party investigation or other process in making a decision under this Policy, though it retains the discretion to take any such outcome into account in determining a Fitness to Practise issue.

## 6. Duties of Students

It  is  the  responsibility  of  each  student  to  familiarise  themselves  with  this  Policy,  specific expectations  of  the  programme  of  study  including  the  specific  SETU  Master  of  Pharmacy Professional  Code  of  Conduct  for  Student  Pharmacists,  and  Core  Competency  Framework  for Pharmacists.

To demonstrate that they are fit to practise, students must understand the following requirements regarding their own health:

- That their health problem(s) may put themselves or others at risk;
- That they seek medical and/or occupational health advice if there is a concern about their health, including their mental health.
- That they accept that they may not be able to assess their own health accurately and be  willing  to  be  referred  for  assessment  by  a  suitably  qualified  practitioner  and  be willing to engage in recommended treatment programmes.
- By  registering  annually  for  their  programme  following  their  first-year  declaration, students are declaring that they believe their health status is such as to allow them to undertake safe and effective practice. If a student's health status changes or potential ill  health  causes concern as to their capacity for safe and effective practice, whether

declared  by  the  student  or  noticed/reported  by  others,  they  may  be  subject  to assessment of their Fitness to Practise under this Policy. Students understand that if the education team become concerned regarding their health, this will be discussed with the student.

Relevant  programmes  in  the  Department  of  Pharmacy  will  require  students  to  undergo  Garda Vetting in accordance  with legislation and  to disclose relevant criminal convictions and prosecutions pending.

This SETU policy will be used in respect of students whose Garda Vetting disclosure gives rise to a fitness to practise concern.  The student must also disclose criminal convictions and prosecutions pending, if any occur during their programme of study that may invalidate or revoke this vetting. Action  may  be  taken  in  respect  of  a  student  under  this  Policy  regardless  of  the  outcome  in criminal proceedings.

## 7. Disability

SETU is committed to equality, diversity and inclusion, for both staff and students, which includes equal opportunities  and  the  support  of  students  with  disabilities.  Students  with  disabilities  are positively  encouraged  to  study  on  programmes  within  the  Department  of  Pharmacy  and reasonable  accommodation  is  provided  where  practicable.  The  Department  can  only  make reasonable accommodation, however, where it knows about any specific health condition and its effects upon the student, and when the disclosure is made in sufficient time to allow necessary supports to be put in place.

It is expected that a student should have the capacity to, (i) assess their own fitness to practise, (ii) review  their  own  fitness  to  practise  and,  (iii)  seek  appropriate  advice  and  explore  reasonable accommodation should anything affect their fitness  to  practise.  If  a  student  remains  unable  to provide  safe  and  effective  practise  despite  reasonable  accommodation,  then  the  fitness  to practise procedure laid down in this Policy may be followed.

## 8. Raising/ Reporting Fitness to Practice Concerns

Any person concerned about the behaviour, health, and/or professional conduct of a student has the  right  to  raise  their  concern.  A  concern  may  be  raised  with  any  staff  member  on  the programme, who should bring this to the attention of the Programme Director and/or Head of Department. In the case of a student engaged in practice placement, the practice educator should be notified who will raise this to the Programme Director and/or Head of Department. Concerns must be clearly outlined, in writing and available supporting evidence included. Where students have concerns for their own fitness to practise, they should discuss the issue with their practice educator  or  Programme  Director.  If  the  matter  has  been  raised  by  a  complainant,  the  person making the complaint (the complainant) should be made aware that:

- Full details of the complaint or concern will be put to the student.
- The student may be given an opportunity to engage with the complainant face to face
